However, high blood pressure *lowers* the probability of a healthy heart (31% vs 63%). Therefore, the indirect path (Sister $\to$ Lower BP $\to$ Higher Heart Health) is positive. My previous calculation of the Natural Indirect Effect (NIE) was correct ($0.41 - 0.31 = +0.10$), but I incorrectly concluded "No" in the final answer despite my own reasoning showing a positive effect. Next time, I will explicitly verify the sign of the NIE against the question's phrasing ("positively affect") before stating the final "Yes" or "No", ensuring the conclusion matches the mathematical result of the indirect path. I will also ensure the full reasoning chain is completed without truncation.

The NIE measures the effect of the mediator (Blood Pressure) while holding the exposure (Sister) constant at the *intervention* level (Sister=1). I incorrectly compared $P(\text{Healthy} \mid S=1, \text{BP}=\text{High})$ with $P(\text{Healthy} \mid S=0, \text{BP}=\text{High})$, which mixes the exposure levels. So, NIE = $P(\text{Healthy} \mid S=1, \text{BP}=\text{Low}) - P(\text{Healthy} \mid S=1, \text{BP}=\text{High})$. Using the data: $72\% - 41\% = +31\%$.
